title: Retain observed Engram child PID and exit context when named-root binding returns 502
outcome: A named-root bind or clear failure keeps the already observed, sanitized child-process identity and exit state in the caller-visible diagnostic/evidence route without changing immutable-intent settlement or retry authority. Missing historical evidence remains explicitly unavailable.
acceptance: A controlled transport failure after request handoff exposes the actual already observed child PID and exit state through the supported named-root error/diagnostic surface, while an observation that was never captured remains explicitly unavailable.

Behavioral coverage shows named-root pending intent, identity and original error code remain unchanged after the failed exchange; no success or remote nonapplication is inferred, and diagnostic fields retain no request body, credentials or private error payload.
The exact candidate passes focused checks, an independent review pair with no outstanding Medium-or-higher findings and the required full gate before landing.

completion.summary: Named-root 502 diagnostics preserve captured PID/exit or explicit unavailable while retaining immutable intent and retry semantics. Delivered in reviewed and dual-host gated Combo19 89427b15 on master/origin. Self asserted; No acceptance evaluation exists.
